newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CSFB sees better Q2 for TVK, keeps "hold".
newsitem.headline: CSFB sees better Q2 for TVK, keeps "hold".

text.p: Higher product prices and lower costs will allow Hungarian chemicals firm TVK to have much better figures in the second quarter of 1997 than in the first one, CS First Boston said, maintaining its "hold" rating.
"Strong polyolefin prices, combined with a sharp fall in naphtha costs, should make Q2 numbers significantly stronger than Q1," Spencer Jakab, analyst at CSFB, said in a company update.

TVK released its earnings report for the January-March period on Monday and reported an unconsolidated IAS net income of 2.748 billion forints as against a net income of 1.717 billion in the corresponding period of 1996.
TVK's consolidated net income of 2.745 billion forints was in line with CSFB's expectations, he said.

Jakab said that while TVK's strong Q1 results were more or less factored into the price, the company's plans to expand its cracker capacity should also add significant value and therefore CSFB raised its forecasts to reflect this.
